result.summary: This PR changes wallet history RPCs (gettransaction, listtransactions, listsinceblock) to stop applying normal all-inputs-wallet-owned accounting to transactions that spend a mix of wallet-owned and foreign inputs. It adds input-ownership caching, a new history-accounting helper, and reports either normal per-output send/fee accounting (when all foreign inputs are known to have zero value) or a single conservative aggregate 'send' entry with no address/vout/fee plus 'receive' entries for wallet-owned outputs. It exposes new fields (involves_mixed_inputs, wallet_debit, wallet_credit) and documents the change in a release note, with substantial functional test coverage added.
result.problem: Wallet history RPCs currently misreport fees and falsely attribute foreign outputs as wallet-initiated sends for transactions like CoinJoins and payjoins where the wallet owns only some inputs, an issue tracked since 2018 in #14136 and felt by users and tools relying on gettransaction/listtransactions for accurate accounting, especially after wallet restore or rescan when transaction-intent metadata is unavailable.

The underlying problem is real but not urgent: no funds are lost, and the PR's own description frames it as a partial fix pending a possibly richer future metadata layer.

result.card: This PR reworks how bitcoind's wallet history RPCs (gettransaction, listtransactions, listsinceblock) report transactions that mix wallet-owned and foreign inputs, such as CoinJoins and payjoins, replacing the current misleading full-fee/full-send accounting with a conservative fallback that reports only what the wallet can prove: wallet debit, wallet credit, and per-output receives, falling back to per-output send/fee accounting only when foreign inputs are provably zero-value. It targets long-standing issue #14136 (open since 2018) about wrong gettransaction info for CoinJoin-like transactions. The design has been substantially reworked once already after a maintainer (achow101) gave a concept NACK saying dropping send entries entirely was 'even more misleading', and another maintainer (murchandamus) left an extensive, still-unanswered 2026-07-15 review raising correctness and wording concerns. The PR needs a rebase and the author has been silent for 70+ days despite a 2026-09-09 maintainer request to respond; it also conflicts with several other open wallet-internals PRs (#35786, #35716, #35501, #27865).
